available_strategies.name: full_stack
available_strategies.purpose: Validation and browser-aligned full field plots.

available_strategies.name: mirror_half
available_strategies.purpose: Solve one end through the middle plate, then mirror across the center plane.
available_strategies.boundary: Mirror plane uses even-potential symmetry, dV/dz = 0, outside fixed conductor cells.
available_strategies.valid_excitation: All bias conductors at the same voltage, or another excitation individually even about the stack center.
available_strategies.invalid_excitation: An arbitrary single-node basis field; only its full-domain reflected partner may be reused.

available_strategies.name: end_repeat_approx
available_strategies.purpose: Solve end-to-first-bias-center and bias-center-to-next-ground-center regions, then copy and mirror them through the stack.
available_strategies.boundary: Cuts use zero-normal-flux at the assumed bias-plate and ground-plate axial symmetry planes.
available_strategies.valid_excitation: Routine equal-voltage all-bias field and total-capacitance screening only.
available_strategies.invalid_excitation: Single-node Maxwell basis fields and differential bias-to-bias capacitance excitations.

checks.name: peak_field
checks.comparison: max absolute field from mirrored half-stack versus full-stack reference

checks.name: peak_location
checks.comparison: peak location should map to the same physical edge class after mirroring

checks.name: mirrored_field_map
checks.comparison: reconstructed full field from the half-stack should match full-stack field samples

notes: Mirror symmetry is exact only when both the idealized geometry and the electrode excitation are reflection-symmetric.
Arbitrary single-node capacitance basis fields use the full domain; a reflected partner field may be reused because reflection maps one physical excitation onto the other.
Repeating-cell reuse is limited to the equal-voltage all-bias field/total-capacitance screen and is not applied to Maxwell basis or differential Cpar solves.
The repeating-cell approximation is the operational default; retain mirror-half and full-stack cases as validation references for finite-stack end effects.
Tolerances allow for discretization and interpolation differences between full and reconstructed grids during solver development.
Axisymmetric r-z model.
HV flow holes are omitted from this first-order field model.
Bias plates are solid discs extending to the axis; they have no center ID.
The core is represented as separate axial pieces divided by the solid bias plates.
All HV conductors are held at the full bias voltage for local field screening.
Current electrostatic solver treats conductors as equipotential boundaries; conductivity and permeability fields are carried for future RF/quasi-static backends.
Ground plate OD is intended to contact the ground tube ID when the tube is included.
HV plate rounding applies to the outer radial edge; ground plate rounding applies to the inner radial edge.

adaptive.note: Mirror-half FEniCSx/Gmsh solve reconstructed onto the full browser r-z grid.

capacitance.description: Node-resolved FEniCSx capacitance matrix from single-node basis-field cross energies plus an all-bias energy check, with the core treated as dielectric.

capacitance_network.matrix_extraction: basis-field cross-energy with exact reflected-field interpolation

bias_to_ground_comparison.interpretation: The middle-only diagonal includes mutual capacitance to every bias plate held at zero volts. The three-state polarization subtraction removes those terms. The one-bias geometry provides an independent case with no bias-to-bias mutual capacitance to subtract.

cg_matrix_plate_count_comparison.repeating_note: Two bias plates have no interior node and three bias plates have only one interior node, so the repeating-interior assumption adds no equivalence beyond exact reflection for this comparison.

solverStatus.reason: FEniCSx is ready and selected by auto mode.

fenicsx.installHint: sudo apt install fenicsx gmsh python3-gmsh python3-dolfinx

equation.strongForm: div(epsilon_r grad(V)) = 0 in cylindrical r-z geometry
equation.dirichlet: HV core and HV plates at bias_voltage_v; ground plates and optional tube at 0 V
equation.natural: Open outer model boundaries use zero-normal-flux unless replaced by a larger grounded boundary.

meshPlan.geometry: Generate the r-z dielectric domain with Gmsh/OpenCASCADE and remove conductor regions as holes.
initialRefinement: Set small Gmsh sizes on rounded HV outer edges.
Set small Gmsh sizes on rounded ground inner edges.
Refine dielectric-interface endpoints near plate overlap boundaries.
adaptiveLoop: Estimate field and/or flux-jump error by cell.
Refine marked cells or remesh with tighter Gmsh size fields.
Stop when peak field and peak location converge.
